newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-STRIKE THREAT STILL LOOMS OVER SPANISH LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STRIKE THREAT STILL LOOMS OVER SPANISH LEAGUE.

text.p: The spectre of a strike is still hanging over Spanish soccer after the players' union demanded that the number of foreigners allowed in each team be reduced from four players to just one by 1999.

The demands of Gerardo Movilla, president of the Association of Spanish Footballers are in total contradiction to current thinking in Europe following the Bosman ruling which removed transfer and eligibility restrictions for footballers across the continent.
Nevertheless Movilla, upset that more than 200 overseas players are now in the Spanish first and second divisions, says: "It's clear that the clubs have abused the system.
Movilla has sent his demands to the Professional Football League, the Spanish Federation and the Superior Sports Council.
Although Movilla hesitates to talk of strike action, the threat of a stoppage has already been used by players this season to create a Christmas break.
Numbers of footballing immigrants have boomed in Spain this season after clubs increased the number of foreigners allowed on the field at one time from three to four.

Just to prove the players' union point, Deportivo Coruna completed the signing of Brazilian striker Luizao from Palmeiras on Tuesday in a deal thought to be worth around 700 million pesetas ($4.86 million).
Luizao becomes the sixth Brazilian at the club joining Rivaldo, Renaldo, Mauro Silva, Donato and Flavio Conceicao at Deportivo, who are currently in third place in the Spanish first division.

La Coruna has been a favoured destination for Brazilians since the arrival of World Cup striker Bebeto in 1992. The local Galician language spoken in the city is similar to the Brazilians' native tongue, Portuguese.
